name: Aerostaticus
description: A star 56 parsecs away, 2.6 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 105140: radius 2.639 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 31.77 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.283) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 105140: effective temperature 8442 +/- 1273 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.052)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 105140: distance 55.866 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.013), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 56 parsecs away, 2.6 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 32 times the Sun's luminosity at 8,442 K, so 2.639 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 105140: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Epsilon Microscopii
quotes.card: Epsilon Microscopii, also named Aerostaticus, is a single, white-hued star in the southern constellationof Microscopium.
quotes.introduction: It is faintly visible to the naked eye with an apparent visual magnitude of 4.71.
